samples.summary: The improved "resolved from" refusal was applied to the driver, but the line that actually appeared in the incident log is printed by the CHILD scorers, and every one of them still says only "does not exist under this root"
samples.evidence: The 2026-08-17 log quoted in the diff and in docs/tasks/active/20260813-eval-scoring-lane-todo.md:335 shows `corpus version "2026-08-10-pilot-reviewed" does not exist under this root` emitted immediately after `score-all: volume-mix.mjs (pilot-01__k1)` — i.e. by a spawned child, not by scoreAll. The driver's own message (score-all.mjs:588) now names the resolved root, but the child-side messages are unchanged and name no path at all: scripts/agent/eval/adapters/coderabbit.mjs:1138, scripts/agent/eval/reliability.mjs:1287, scripts/agent/eval/cost-latency.mjs:1086, scripts/agent/eval/segmentation.mjs:1294, scripts/agent/eval/report.mjs:1573. complementarity.mjs:1097 prints `args.root` verbatim, which for a relative value is equally ambiguous. Since the driver preflights the same corpus and now resolves the path, the only realistic future reader of a corpus refusal is still one of these child messages — so the diagnostic half of the fix lands on the site that did not misdiagnose anything.

samples.summary: scoreAll's failure contract for a non-string `root` changed: `path.resolve(rootArg)` now runs before `new EvalStore(root)`, so EvalStore's deliberate `requireRoot` refusal is no longer what a caller sees
samples.evidence: scripts/agent/eval/store.mjs:273-281 (`requireRoot`) exists specifically to refuse a non-string/blank root with the "there is no default…" message, and it already did `path.resolve` itself — so the store was never the site of the cwd bug. Moving resolution ahead of construction means any truthy non-string root (a number, an array, a Buffer from a future programmatic caller) now escapes as a raw `TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE]` from node:path instead of the module's own refusal. Today's only production caller is main() at score-all.mjs:731, which passes a parsed string, so this is a latent contract change rather than a live break; a `typeof rootArg !== "string"` refuse before line 578 restores it.
searchedFor: Grep scoreAll callers repo-wide (only score-all.mjs:730 and score-all.test.mjs)

samples.summary: The two new tests mutate process-wide cwd inside a test file whose other 40 tests share the same process; the invariant "no test in this file depends on cwd" is now load-bearing and unstated
samples.evidence: score-all.test.mjs:679 and :729 call `process.chdir()`. Every other path in the file is absolute today (HERE at :58, WORKFLOW at :59, `source()` at :92, mkdtempSync roots), so nothing breaks now — but node:test runs the tests of one file in one process, so any later relative-path test, or a lane switched to in-process isolation (where `process.chdir` is unavailable in worker threads), fails for a reason that has nothing to do with the test that changed the cwd. The `--test` lane asserted in eval/test-lane.test.mjs:104-127 is what pins the current process-per-file behaviour.
searchedFor: checked score-all.test.mjs:1-120 for relative path usage
